judgement.title: APM PMS Q&A SOP: the weekly session, run on Saturday 10 October 2026 on Friday 9 October 2026 closes
judgement.heading: Arteche | Core Investment | 3.28% of the fund's capital in 2 tranches
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** O. Industrials and capital goods. Industry RS 79 at the Friday 9 October reading (66 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** O.4. Electrical equipment, grid and automation (re-drawn on 6 October). Sector RS 69 at the 30 September month-end on the new group (62 on Friday's daily reading). Its other companies: Alfen (Stock RS 39, held), Cenergy (89, in the Pool), Fastned (98, in the Pool), ABB (72), Siemens (59), Schneider Electric (54), and 10 more
- **Cohort:** grid equipment makers for power networks. The cohort's relative strength 45 (23 four weeks earlier), 6 companies: Alfen (39, held), Cembre (78), Landis+Gyr (56), Pfisterer (18), R&S Group (8)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock fell 3.6% to EUR 34.70; the market was flat, so it was all its own move, half its usual size (about 7.5%), in line with its sector's companies (median -3.9%). Over 20 sessions it rose 15.3%, an own move of 16.3%, its usual size
  - No public news explains either; the week matched the grid sector's
- **The sector and cohort:** the re-drawn sector reads 69 at the month-end, where the old grid sector read 52, and the cohort's relative strength rose to 45 from 23. Arteche's own Stock RS (95 at the month-end) leads both
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates +33% and target prices +33%, both from zero at the end of August; Sell-side Momentum A, better than a month and three months ago
- **The reading that matters: relative price.** It was 19% below its 52-week high at the 30 September month-end; on Friday's prices 24% below, so the share price is less than 1% above the trigger price. The rule reads it only on 30 October

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** hold; none of the six Sell Criteria is met at the readings the rule uses
- **Selling:** the nearest trigger is the relative 52W high trigger at about EUR 34.40, less than 1% below Friday's EUR 34.70, read at the 30 October month-end; if the price is at or below it then, with the market flat, the whole holding sells at the 3 November session
  - *About even odds, or a little worse:* its usual own move over 20 sessions is 17% either way and the price is at the line. The 30% level is EUR 26.39, 24% below
- **Adding:** allowed by the rule (3.40% of room); not wanted, because an add at the line of a whole-holding trigger could be sold with the rest three weeks later, and the memo's entry level is near EUR 22

**What we could lose:** about 0.03% of the fund's capital, to the relative 52W high trigger (0.79% to the 30% level)

**Experiment: which stocks Arteche's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Siemens Energy** (same sector): 0.41 and 0.28, moderate
- **Legrand** (same sector): 0.38 and 0.35, moderate
- **Prysmian** (same sector): 0.35 and 0.20, weak
- **ACS** (same country of listing): 0.29 and 0.26, weak
- **My reading:** look at Legrand and Siemens Energy first; on the re-drawn sector Arteche's weeks now track the electrification names a little, where on Tuesday nothing explained them

**The Investment Analyst's memo (the record of 10 September, republished 1 October, at EUR 29.5; no digest has been written)**

- **Decided:** neutral on the shares and bullish on the business; park, with a price trigger at about EUR 22 and an event trigger at the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation in October or November 2026. The park is on price, not on the quality gate
- **Must happen:** the 2026 guidance delivered (revenue EUR 565m to 590m, margin before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of 16.3% to 17.8%) and a plan that justifies the multiple
- **Main risk:** the valuation, 31.5 times current earnings at the 100th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history, on a free float of 12.5%
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** not stated in the parts I can read without a digest; the TSR/Valuation reading of F says the expected return at today's price is below 10% a year, against our 20% bar
- **Next test:** the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation; the 30 October month-end reading of relative price

**My judgement:** neutral on the position, medium conviction: a strong holding in a recovering cohort, sitting at the line of a month-end trigger; hold, do not add, and let the rule decide on 30 October.

- **Counter-case:** the trigger is a single month-end snapshot, and a 16% own move in 20 sessions is ordinary for this stock, so a fire on 30 October could sell a cohort leader on noise; if the Strategic Plan lands well before the month-end, an overrule with that reason is defensible

**What would change my view:** the 30 October reading of relative price (the trigger at about EUR 34.40 with the market flat); the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation

- **Cohort:** power grid infrastructure equipment (smart metering, cables and grid automation). The cohort's relative strength 86 (61 four weeks earlier), 4 companies: Alfen (53, held), Cenergy (93, in the Pool), Landis+Gyr (53)

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock fell 1.4%; the market's 0.8% fall explains 0.7% of it, so its own move was 0.7%, a tenth of its usual size (about 7.6%). Over 20 sessions it rose 16.5%, an own move of 18.6%, about its usual size (17.1%). The rise came on 22 to 25 September
  - The 5.8% fall on 1 October came on the day the market fell 1.3% on bond yields. No public news explains either
- **The sector and cohort:** the grid-equipment cohort's relative strength rose to 86 from 61 four weeks ago, while the wider grid sector's fell to 52 at the month-end (97 at the end of June). The market is paying for the cohort, not the sector.
  - That is why Arteche's Stock RS (95 at the month-end) stays high while its sector reading sits two points from the Pool's line
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates +33% and target prices +33%, both from zero at the end of August: the analysts have been raising since the 28 July half-year results and guidance (revenue EUR 565m to 590m, EBITDA EUR 92m to 100m)

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** hold; none of the six Sell Criteria is met, and the stock leads its cohort (Stock RS 95)
- **Selling:** the nearest trigger is the relative 52W high trigger at about EUR 34.46, <u>about 2% below Monday's EUR 35.30</u>, read only at the 30 October month-end; with the market flat a 2% fall by then fires it and sells the whole holding at the 3 November session.
  - *Near even odds:* Arteche's usual own move over 20 sessions is 17% either way, so a 2% cushion is about a coin toss. The 30% level is EUR 26.39, 25% below
- **Adding:** allowed by the rule (3.40% of room; the next add of 1.67% takes Industrials and capital goods to 23.97% of capital); not wanted today, because an add 2% from a whole-holding trigger could be sold with the rest four weeks later, and the memo parks on price with an entry level near EUR 22.
  - Wait for the 30 October reading

**What we could lose:** about 0.08% of the fund's capital, to the relative 52W high trigger (0.83% to the 30% level)

**The Investment Analyst's memo (the record of 10 September, republished 1 October, at EUR 29.5)**

- **Decided:** neutral on the shares and bullish on the business; park, with a price trigger at about EUR 22 and an event trigger at the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation in October or November 2026. The park is on price, not on the quality gate
- **Must happen:** the 2026 guidance delivered (revenue EUR 565m to 590m, EBITDA margin 16.3% to 17.8%) and a plan that justifies the multiple

- **Counter-case:** the trigger is a month-end snapshot of relative price, and a 20% own move in 20 sessions is ordinary for this stock, so a marginal fire on a flat day would sell a cohort leader on noise; the strongest case against the rule is to overrule a marginal fire if the Strategic Plan is well received
